title: Safe frying: buns, doughnuts and fish rolls
course_title: Basic Baking & Snacks Production: Hands-On Small Batches for Sale

say: Safe frying: buns, doughnuts and fish rolls.
This is the video for module 2 of Basic Baking and Snacks Production.
Hot oil burns deeper than boiling water, and an oil fire spreads in seconds. Use a deep, heavy pot on a stable burner, with the handle turned inwards.

panel.heading: Set up a safe frying station
items: Deep, heavy pot, handle turned inwards
Oil only one third to half full
Fitting lid within arm's reach
Water, wet cloths and children away
Heat gradually; check with a thermometer

say: Fill it no more than one third to half full. Food added to a full pot makes the oil rise and overflow onto the flame.

say: Heat the oil gradually and check it with a frying thermometer. Most snacks fry well between about 160 and 180 degrees. If oil smokes, turn the heat down at once.

panel.rule: Never leave heating oil unattended, not even to answer the door.

say: Never throw water on burning oil. It turns to steam instantly and throws burning oil out of the pot.

cards.d: Water on burning oil turns to steam and throws burning oil out of the pot.
Heat off if safe. Slide a fitting lid over the pot and leave it until cool. Do not carry it.
Cool under cool running water for 20 minutes. Seek help if larger than a small coin.

say: Turn off the heat if you safely can, slide a fitting lid or fire blanket over the pot, and leave it covered until cool. Do not carry the pot outside. If the fire spreads, get everyone out and call the fire service.

say: For a burn, cool it under cool running water for 20 minutes. Get medical help for anything larger than a small coin, or on the face, hands or joints.

say: Buns use baking powder, not yeast, so there is no waiting. Mix 500 g of flour with sugar, baking powder, salt and nutmeg, then rub in 60 g of margarine until it looks like breadcrumbs.

panel.heading: Nigerian buns, about 24 pieces
items: Rub 60 g margarine into the dry mix
Add eggs and milk: thick, sticky dough
Oil at about 160 to 170 degrees
Drop 40 g pieces gently, close to the oil
Fry 6 to 8 minutes; break one open to check

say: Add beaten eggs and milk a little at a time, until the dough is thick and sticky. It should not pour like puff-puff batter.

say: Buns are thick, so use slightly cooler oil, about 160 to 170 degrees, so the inside cooks before the outside darkens.

say: Drop pieces of about 40 g close to the oil surface, so they do not splash. Fry a few at a time and let the oil recover.

say: Fry 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden, not very dark. Break one open: no wet dough inside. Afterwards, strain and store your oil, with separate oil for fish.

say: Doughnuts are softer than buns, but yeast needs warmth and patience. Use lukewarm milk, never hot, because hot liquid kills yeast.
To judge proving, press a floured finger about 1 cm into the dough. If the dent springs back quickly, it needs more time.

If it springs back slowly and leaves a small dent, it is ready. If it does not spring back at all, it is over-proved and will soak up oil. Fry at about 170 to 175 degrees, then roll in sugar while warm.
For example, Funke in Ibadan has an order for 45 doughnuts at 9:30 am. One batch gives about 15, so she needs 3.

panel.heading: Three staggered doughnut batches
items: Order: 45 doughnuts, collected 9:30 am
Batch A mixed at 6:00, fried 8:00 to 8:15
Batch B 30 minutes later, fried 8:30
Batch C fried 9:00 to 9:15

say: Batch A is mixed at 6:00, proved, cut, proved again, and fried from 8:00 to 8:15.

say: Fish filling is moist, protein-rich food that bacteria love. Buy fresh fish, keep it cool, and use it the same day.

panel.heading: A safe fish roll filling
items: Fresh fish, kept cool, used the same day
Boil until it flakes, opaque to the bone
Remove every bone: check twice
Fry with onion and pepper until fairly dry
Spread thin to cool, then refrigerate

say: Boil it until the flesh flakes easily and is opaque to the bone.

panel.heading: A safe fish roll filling
items: Fresh fish, kept cool, used the same day
Boil until it flakes, opaque to the bone
Remove every bone: check twice
Fry with onion and pepper until fairly dry
Spread thin to cool, then refrigerate

say: Remove the skin and every bone. Run your fingers through it twice, because a bone is a choking hazard.

panel.heading: A safe fish roll filling
items: Fresh fish, kept cool, used the same day
Boil until it flakes, opaque to the bone
Remove every bone: check twice
Fry with onion and pepper until fairly dry
Spread thin to cool, then refrigerate

say: Fry it with onion and pepper until hot and fairly dry. A wet filling makes rolls burst.

panel.heading: A safe fish roll filling
items: Fresh fish, kept cool, used the same day
Boil until it flakes, opaque to the bone
Remove every bone: check twice
Fry with onion and pepper until fairly dry
Spread thin to cool, then refrigerate

say: Spread it thin to cool fast, then refrigerate. Wrap with cold filling, seal with a fork, and fry at about 165 to 175 degrees.
Sell fish rolls the same day, labelled as containing fish, egg and wheat.

panel.heading: A safe fish roll filling

panel.rule: Cooked filling: no more than 2 hours at room temperature in total.

say: To remember. Set up a safe frying station every time. Never use water on an oil fire. Fry in small loads. Trust the finger test. And cook fish filling fully, debone it twice and cool it fast.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Pot one third to half full, lid within reach
Never water on an oil fire: cover it
Small loads; let the oil recover
Finger test tells you when dough is proved
Fish filling: cook, debone twice, cool fast

say: Now practise. Fry a batch of buns and record the temperature and time of each load. Make and time a doughnut batch. Then make a half batch of fish rolls, recording when the filling was cooked, cooled and refrigerated.
